https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox1.png

The '''Music Box''' plays music in your home on voice command. It holds the shard's library of player compositions: free songs, songs you have bought, and your own. Composers publish their songs to it and are paid when players buy them.

__TOC__

==General Usage==
Buy a music box from any Bard NPC, lock it down in your home, and double-click it. It plays your whole playlist from start to finish, then stops. Double-click it again to stop it sooner.

Give your music box a name: single-click it and choose the rename option. You then speak to it by name, as you would to a smart speaker (its designer named his "Alexa"):

 Alexa, play Douce Dame Jolie
 Alexa, next
 Alexa, previous
 Alexa, repeat
 Alexa, shuffle
 Alexa, loop

You never need a song's whole name: a few words of it are enough, and the music box works out which song you mean, using Angel Island's Intelligent Dialogue System. ''Alexa, help'' lists every command.

To see what music is available, say ''list'':

 Alexa, list

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox2.png

Yellow titles are yours to play: free songs, songs you have bought, and songs you composed. Red titles are premium songs, which cost gold.

===Browsing the Library===
With many songs, a list scrolls by quickly. To browse them all in a window instead, say ''library'' (or ''browse''), or choose '''Look At''' from the music box's context menu:

 Alexa, library

The window shows every song, 11 to a page, with tabs:
* '''All''': every song.
* '''Mine''': the songs you can play in full: ones you bought or composed, and free ones. Songs you submitted that are waiting for review are here too, marked '''Pending''' in red; only you see them here until they are approved.
* '''Free''': free songs, including Napster tracks.
* '''Premium''': songs that cost gold.
* '''New''': the latest releases, the same ones ''new'' lists.
The authors are listed on the left: choose one to see only their songs. Each song shows what it is to you: '''Owned''', '''Free''', '''Napster''', its price, or '''Pending'''.

Press the arrow beside a song to play it: in full if it is yours or free, otherwise a short sample. Press '''Buy''' beside a premium song to buy it (you are asked to confirm the price), and '''Stop''' to stop the music. Anyone near a music box may browse its library, but playing and buying need access to the house, just like speaking to the box.

To hear a premium song before buying it, ask the music box to play it:

 Alexa, play strut

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox3.png

It plays a 10-second sample. To buy the song:

 Alexa, buy strut

The music box walks you through the purchase:

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox4.png

When you agree, the price is taken from your bank (or your shared bank accounts) and paid into the composer's bank, here Pastor Wydstrin's. In this screenshot the player has named the music box ''Bach'', and asked for the song by part of its name.

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox5.png

The song is now in your '''library''' and your '''playlist''', ready to play:
* Your library is every song you have access to.
* Your playlist is the songs from your library that the music box plays. You might take the Christmas songs out of it in July. ''Remove'' takes a song out; ''add'' puts it back.

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox6.png

Say the music box's name, then the command. Several commands have a second word that does the same thing.

|-

|-

|-

|-
| resume (or continue) || Resumes after a pause.
|-

|-

|-

|-
| shuffle || Shuffles your playlist.
|-
| list || Lists the songs. ''list'' with words lists the songs that have all of them in their title, composer, About or tags (''list christmas'', ''list rock'' finds a song tagged ''classic rock''); ''list by'' with a name lists that composer's songs.
|-
| library (or browse) || Opens the library window: every song by tab and author, with play, buy and stop buttons (see Browsing the Library).
|-
| new (or what's new) || Lists the latest releases, newest first, with when each was approved or remastered: everything from the last week, and always at least the five most recent.

|-

|-

|-
| remaster || Asks to replace one of your approved songs with a new version.
|-
| rename || Renames the music box.
|-
| help || Lists the commands.
|}

===Naming a Song===
Say all of a song's title, or enough of it: ''play gilded'' finds a song with ''gilded'' in its title, and ''play kpdh golden'' finds ''Golden (KPDH)'' (the words in any order; capitals and punctuation don't matter). An exact title always wins. Words a title doesn't hold all of don't match it: if no title holds them, the box says it doesn't know that song, and may suggest one that's close (''Did you mean Golden (KPDH)?'').

When several songs match, '''play''', '''add''' and '''remove''' take the closest (the shortest title) and say so; say more of the title for another. '''buy''' never guesses: it lists the songs that match, and you say more of the title, or the song's number (''buy 0x4003F1D0''), shown in the list.

==Instructions for Composers==
The Music Box is how composers share and sell their work across the shard.

# Write your song in a composition book and transcribe it into [[Sheet Music]]. Set its name and price at the top of the composition with # Song: and # Price: (a price of 0 makes it free). See [[Sheet Music#Settings|Settings]] for every setting.
# Single-click your music box and choose '''Add''', or say ''submit'' (or just ''add''). Target your sheet music.

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox8.png

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox9.png

The song's # Author: is the credit its listeners see, and the gold from its sales goes to you. So the author may be your own name, any of your characters (on any of your accounts, or someone who plays from your home), or credit such as ''Beethoven'' or a band, but not another player: the box refuses a song that names another player's character as its author. An author's name is at most 40 characters. When the author isn't you or another of your characters, the box names you too, as its arranger: ''Rooster by Alice in Chains, arranged by Gud'Gul.''

Your song is now in the shard-wide library, not just your own music box, and goes into a review queue. Staff review songs to keep out offensive content, not to judge their quality (songs can have lyrics). While it waits, you can still play it on your own music box: it is in your playlist, and the box says it is pending approval. Once approved, it appears for every player: free songs in their libraries, premium songs as red titles they can sample and buy.

Each approved song earns you [[Music Composition#Music Karma|Music Karma]], and so does every sale and every play.

===After Review===
You're told what staff decided the next time you use a music box, any music box (walk up to it, double-click it, open its menu or speak to it): ''Your song Bombshell was approved!'', or that it wasn't approved and why. Say ''status'' to see all your songs at once:

 Alexa, status

Each song is listed as waiting for review, approved (with the date), or not approved with the reason staff gave. Your sales follow. A long list scrolls by quickly: ''status rejected'' shows only the songs that weren't approved, with their reasons (''status pending'' and ''status approved'' work the same way).

Staff may rename a song in the library, so that every title says whose music it is: ''Creep (Radiohead)'', ''Dungeon Strut (Original)'', ''Greensleeves (Traditional)''. You're told at your next music box visit, or by ''status'': ''Your song Radiohead_-_Creep is now listed in the music library as Creep (Radiohead).'' It's still your song, with its sales and its sheet music; only the name changed. Staff may also set or tidy a song's # About: and # Tags: (see [[Sheet Music#Settings|Settings]]); that changes only how it's described and found, and isn't news.

To publish a new version of an approved song, say ''remaster''. A book that still has the song's old name works: the new version takes the name the library uses now.

The library is permanent and not tied to your account: once a song is in, it stays available to other players. If the character who composed a song is deleted, the song becomes free.

===Napster Tracks===
A song transcribed with ''# Napster: True'' is passed hand to hand instead of sold. Anyone who has a copy of its sheet music can add it to their own music box, which gives them the song (the sheet is used up). Other players hear only a sample, and are told to get a copy from the composer.

===Getting Paid===
When a player buys your song, the price goes straight into your bank. Say ''sales'' to see your totals:

 Alexa, sales

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox10.png

If your bank box can't take the gold, the sale is recorded as a credit to you instead, shown in your sales. Credits are paid the next time you use a music box, any music box: walk up to it, double-click it, open its menu or speak to it. The gold goes into your bank, and you're told how much. If your bank box is still full, you're told the gold is waiting: make room, then visit a music box again.

Credits are paid only to the character who earned them, on the shard where they were earned. If that character is deleted, or the music library moves to another shard, the credit is not paid.

Say ''purchases'' to see the songs you have bought:

 Alexa, purchases

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox11.png

==Leaderboard==
The Music Box records each composer's sales and the gold they have earned. The leaderboard at your local bank shows them.

https://game-master.net/images/wiki/musicbox/musicbox12.png

==Staff Reference==
Staff use these commands to run the library. Players can't use them.

{| class="wikitable"
! Say !! What it does !! Access
|-
| review || Plays the next song waiting for review, then asks: Approve, Deny or Delete. Deny asks for a reason (TooLong, TooShort, Inappropriate, Duplicate or Other); Other asks for a one-line note to the composer (up to 100 characters). The composer is told at their next music box visit. || Owner
|-
| approve ''song'' || Approves a song waiting for review: it becomes available to every player. ''approve *'' approves every song waiting for review, after you confirm (type Approve). || Owner
|-
| deny ''song'' || Rejects a song waiting for review. ''deny *'' rejects every song waiting for review, after you confirm (type Deny). || Owner
|-
| delete ''song'' || Removes a song from the library, after you confirm (type Delete): the box names the song first. ''delete *'' removes every song, on Test Center only, after you confirm (type Delete). || Owner
|-
| find ''song'' || Shows a song's serial number, owner, and name. || Owner
|-
| dupe ''song'' || Puts a copy of a song's sheet music in your backpack. || Seer
|-
| flushall || Removes every song, everywhere. || Owner, Test Center only
|}
Approve, deny and delete never guess: when several songs match the name (see [[#Naming a Song|Naming a Song]]), the box lists them with their serial numbers and does nothing; say more of the title, or the serial (''delete 0x4003F1D0''). Approve and deny consider only songs waiting for review.

Players trusted with music review use their own command, which needs no music box: see [[#Reviewing Music|Reviewing Music]].

===Importing Songs===
'''[MusicImport''' (Administrators, anywhere) adds the song files (.rzr) in the server's ''Data\Music Import'' folder to the library, approved: a new song at the price in its file (''[MusicImport free'': free), a song the library already has (the same notes) left as it is, and a new version of a song imported before replacing it. A file that can't be a song is refused with the reason. Imported songs pay no one (no one here composed them): their price leaves the economy, and their sales and plays earn no one gold or points. It's how another shard brings in the [https://game-master.net/AimsMusic.html Angel Island Music Library] (''Download all''), and works with any song file.

==Reviewing Music==
Some players are asked to help staff review new songs. A reviewer is still an ordinary player: the '''[MusicReview''' command is the only thing that changes, and it works on every shard, wherever you are.

Review keeps offensive content out of the library. It doesn't judge quality: a song that is rough but harmless should be approved.

===Reviewing songs===
List the songs awaiting review, on every shard:

 [MusicReview list

Each song has a number, with its title, composer, home shard and the date it was submitted. Take them in any order.

To hear song 2:

 [MusicReview listen 2

A review copy goes into your backpack and starts playing; double-click it to hear it again. It disappears after 10 minutes, and it can't be added to a music box.

Then decide:

 [MusicReview approve 2
 [MusicReview deny 3

Deny asks why, as a music box does: '''TooLong''', '''TooShort''', '''Inappropriate''', '''Duplicate''' or '''Other'''. Other asks for a note to the composer (one line, up to 100 characters), and it needs one: a reason the composer can't act on is no use to them. Every denial has a reason; press Esc at either question and nothing is denied.

If you know the reason already, type it: ''[MusicReview deny 3 Duplicate'', or ''[MusicReview deny 4 Other Please put your own name in Arranged by.'' (words that aren't a reason are the note, with the reason Other).

===What happens next===
Your decision is recorded at once and applied by the song's home shard within 5 minutes. The composer is told the next time they use a music box, with your reason and note. Composers aren't told who reviewed their song.

Numbers come from your own last ''list'', so another reviewer's list never changes yours. Until a decision is applied, the song stays on the list marked with who decided it (''approved by Galois, applies within 5 minutes''), and nobody can decide it a second time.

''[MusicReview help'' lists the commands. On Test Center you can list and listen, but decisions are made on the live shards.

===Review notices===
While songs await review, reviewers and staff who are online are told every 5 minutes, for every shard:

 [Music System] 4 songs awaiting review: Angel Island 1, Mortalis 1, Siege Perilous 2 ([MusicReview list; [MusicReview pause quiets these).

Songs already decided aren't counted. To quiet the notices for an hour, say ''[MusicReview pause'' (or ''[MusicReview pause 30'' for 30 minutes, up to 24 hours); ''[MusicReview resume'' turns them back on.

===For Owners===
Owners can always review. To make a player a reviewer, use their account name: the list is shared by every shard and covers all of the account's characters.

{| class="wikitable"
! Command !! What it does
|-
| [MusicReview add ''account'' || Makes the account a reviewer.
|-
| [MusicReview remove ''account'' || Takes the account off the list.
|-
| [MusicReview reviewers || Lists the reviewers.
|}
==History==
The Music Box was designed and built by Adam Ant in 2022, inspired by his Amazon Echo: hence "Alexa". See [[Music Composition#History and Credits|History and Credits]].
